chapter_keywords: a record of a mortal's journey to immortality
chapter_seo_title: RMJI Ch. 512: Han Li's Ancient Treasures Crush Two Core Formation Cultivators
chapter_meta_description: Han Li springs a trap on two Star Palace cultivators, butchering them with the Five Elements Ring's binding power. An invisible observer lurks beneath the waves.
og_title: RMJI Ch. 512 — The Ancient Treasure That Breaks Core Formation
og_description: Han Li reveals the Five Elements Ring’s lockdown property and slaughters two Core Formation cultivators without giving them a chance to fight back.
twitter_title: RMJI Ch. 512 — The Might of Ancient Treasures
twitter_description: Han Li kills two Core Formation cultivators, loots their treasures, and calls out a hidden observer. Cold. Efficient. Mortal Stream at its finest.

lore_anchors.definition: A self-refined Core Formation treasure that generates black mist which can induce illusions; effective against cultivators of equal or slightly higher rank.
A binding-type ancient treasure that can appear on a target invisibly and suppress their mana entirely, rendering even Core Formation cultivators helpless.
A magic weapon from a bygone era, far more powerful than modern self-refined tools; extremely rare among Core Formation cultivators and often a trump card.
A lightning element infused into Han Li’s Azure Bamboo Cloudswarm Swords, granting them immense destructive power against demonic and evil entities; currently depleted.
A treasure refined into the cultivator’s core, connected to their primordial spirit; abandoning it damages cultivation and soul.
The third major cultivation realm, where a cultivator condenses their foundation into a Golden Core; lifespan extends to ~500 years.
A type of cultivation art that deceives the senses or traps the mind in a fabricated reality; the Illusion Inkstone specializes in this.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is an ancient treasure (古宝)?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Ancient treasures are magic weapons from a lost era, far more powerful than modern self-refined tools; they are extremely rare among Core Formation cultivators and often serve as triumph cards.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why couldn’t Han Li’s swords break the barrier?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Without the Evil-Slaying Divine Lightning, his Azure Bamboo Cloudswarm Swords are still newly cultivated and lack mature power; he relied on the Five Elements Ring to bypass the barrier instead.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the hidden observer in the sea?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not revealed in this chapter; a mysterious figure who was watching the fight and is now called out by Han Li.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Five Elements Ring’s main ability?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It can appear on a target invisibly, ignoring common defensive measures, and suppress their mana completely, leaving them helpless.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the burly man abandon his natal treasure?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was desperate to escape and knew the seal was already trapped by Han Li’s basket; saving his life took priority over preserving his core treasure.
